investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T18:58–19:05Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new remote-agent pods. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json line 256 to fail entirely. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible peer-pod nodes. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T19:03–19:05Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0/6 nodes available for scheduling. Because the remote agent pod never became schedulable, the eval probe timed out after ~148 s and produced zero evidence, violating the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract which requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. With no preemption victims available and preemption not helpful on the affinity-mismatched nodes, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in Unschedulable state. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the probe calls createAgent (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) which submits a pod that never schedules, so the probe times out and returns no evidence, causing the contract validation to fail on all 5 required fields.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads consuming that resource, leaving no capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes may have lost a required label or taint that previously allowed remote-agent pods to schedule on them, reducing the eligible node pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes. This would compound the capacity problem.

TERTIARY — Stuck or leaked remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user-initiated agents may not have been cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 implies cleanup is attempted, but leaked pods from failed cleanups could hold capacity), leaving fewer slots for new probes.

LOWER — Cluster node count reduction: one or more kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been cordoned, drained, or removed, shrinking available capacity without a corresponding workload reduction.
